scenarios.hypothesis: A declared synthetic dependency can resolve from a neighboring mock namespace or mirror when source precedence is ambiguous, causing the selected artifact identity to diverge from the intended internal source contract.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use two local mock namespaces containing inert archives with the same synthetic package name but distinct digests, then capture resolver output and selected digest without contacting any public registry or third-party namespace.
scenarios.positive_control: With explicit scoped source policy pointing to the intended local namespace, the resolver must select the expected synthetic source and immutable digest while the legitimate dependency build continues to succeed.
scenarios.negative_control: When the neighboring mock source is presented without authorization, the corrected resolver policy must reject or ignore it even though the logical package name and version label remain identical.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would require publishing a look-alike package, reserving a public namespace, altering an external registry or mirror, or causing any third party to resolve the synthetic package.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, explicit namespace/source policy and immutable artifact binding must select only the intended local source, reject neighboring synthetic sources, and preserve the legitimate dependency resolution path.
scenarios.declared_requirement: The fixture declares one synthetic dependency by logical name and version range, while the evidence ledger records that this declaration alone does not identify the authoritative namespace, source, or artifact bytes.
scenarios.source_resolution_policy: The expected policy binds the synthetic package scope to one local mock registry or mirror, defines precedence and fallback behavior explicitly, and fails closed when the selected source falls outside that policy.
scenarios.selected_namespace_source: Resolver evidence records the exact selected namespace, local registry or mirror identity, canonical upstream identity when applicable, and the policy generation that caused that source to win resolution.
scenarios.selected_artifact_identity: The selected artifact is represented by an inert local archive digest plus synthetic package metadata so the review can distinguish same-name or same-version artifacts without executing untrusted code.
scenarios.immutable_pin_integrity_state: The fixture records whether the selected artifact is bound by exact digest or equivalent immutable identity and treats a mutable version label, tag, or mirror alias as insufficient identity evidence by itself.
scenarios.provenance_verifier_decision: The local verifier records whether the artifact digest, expected source and synthetic publisher/build authority satisfy policy, preventing a checksum-only success from being mistaken for authorized provenance.
scenarios.install_build_hook: This case disables optional install and build hooks or uses an inert deterministic no-op hook so resolver and namespace behavior remain the only material variable under test.
scenarios.toolchain_build_environment: The toolchain and build environment are fixed to one deterministic local fixture identity so platform or compiler drift cannot explain a change in selected dependency artifact identity.
scenarios.ci_principal_trust_context: The resolver executes under one synthetic trusted build principal with no release credentials, while the evidence records that CI identity is held constant and is not the suspected cause of source selection.
scenarios.cache_reuse_input_binding: Resolver caches are disabled or isolated by fixture generation so stale metadata or cross-context cache reuse cannot explain why the neighboring synthetic namespace or artifact was selected.
scenarios.produced_artifact_identity: A deterministic local build emits an inert output digest that incorporates the selected dependency digest, allowing the review to observe whether wrong-source resolution propagates into produced artifact identity.
scenarios.release_signing_publishing_authority: No external publishing occurs; a fake local release authority may attest the deterministic output only after source and artifact identity checks pass, keeping release authority separate from resolver behavior.
scenarios.distributed_artifact_identity: Any distributed artifact in this case is a local fixture copy whose digest is compared with the produced artifact, ensuring later transfer does not introduce a second unexplained identity change.
scenarios.deployed_runtime_artifact_identity: The bounded target records only the inert local artifact digest or metadata marker, so deployment identity can be checked without executing package code or modifying production runtime state.
scenarios.bounded_effect: The maximum allowed effect is selection of the wrong inert synthetic archive and a changed deterministic local output digest; no public package resolution, credential use, or third-party execution is permitted.
scenarios.lifecycle_revocation_update_generation: The source-policy generation is fixed during the primary test, then advanced in a control to confirm stale resolver state cannot continue authorizing a source that the corrected policy has removed.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold package name, version label, toolchain, CI principal, and build inputs constant while switching only the source namespace or immutable artifact digest, then verify the selected identity follows that single change.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude documented mirror equivalence, platform-specific resolution, stale resolver metadata, cache reuse, lockfile regeneration, and test-fixture contamination before attributing the result to source or namespace ambiguity.
scenarios.evidence_level: A deterministic wrong-source selection or identity collision supports SC1 or SC2; inert wrong-artifact acceptance can support SC3, but higher levels require bounded downstream effect and complete causal binding.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Evidence must stop below SC4 if the fixture only proves resolver ambiguity or inert wrong-artifact acceptance; no claim about real public dependency confusion or downstream victims is allowed from this case.

scenarios.hypothesis: A security-relevant build hook, fetched toolchain, cache entry, or artifact produced by a lower-trust synthetic CI principal can influence a trusted build output without being represented correctly in provenance or trust policy.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use a deterministic local build with inert source files, one synthetic build hook or toolchain marker, trust-separated fake CI principals, and local cache fixtures; compare produced digests and provenance records only.
scenarios.positive_control: A trusted synthetic CI principal using the intended immutable toolchain, build hook, dependency identities, and trust-partitioned cache must produce the expected deterministic artifact and complete provenance record.
scenarios.negative_control: An untrusted synthetic PR principal, neighboring toolchain identity, altered inert build hook, or untrusted cache entry must be rejected, rebuilt, or produce a clearly lower-trust artifact that cannot enter the trusted release path.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop if proving the hypothesis would require exposing real CI secrets, reusing production runner state, modifying an external cache, uploading artifacts into a live release pipeline, or executing unknown third-party build code.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, provenance and trust policy must bind every material build input and producer trust context, reject unverifiable lower-trust outputs, and preserve deterministic trusted builds with intended cache reuse.
scenarios.declared_requirement: The fixture declares a small synthetic dependency graph whose identities are fixed so the experiment can focus on whether build hooks, toolchain state, cache provenance, and CI trust are represented in the final artifact chain.
scenarios.source_resolution_policy: All dependencies resolve from one local deterministic source policy with immutable digests, removing namespace ambiguity from the primary experiment while keeping resolver evidence available as a control.
scenarios.selected_namespace_source: The selected sources are fixed local fixture identities recorded in the build manifest, ensuring any output divergence is not explained by a different registry, mirror, or package namespace.
scenarios.selected_artifact_identity: Every selected dependency uses an inert digest-addressed artifact, and those digests are written into the build evidence so build-input drift can be separated from resolver or source-selection drift.
scenarios.immutable_pin_integrity_state: Dependencies, build image, toolchain marker, and relevant fetched inputs are either digest pinned or deliberately varied one at a time, with the evidence noting which input is immutable and which is under test.
scenarios.provenance_verifier_decision: The synthetic provenance verifier checks produced artifact digest, source revision, dependency identities, toolchain/build environment, workflow identity, and CI trust class before treating the output as release-eligible.
scenarios.install_build_hook: One inert deterministic build hook changes a metadata marker in the output when enabled, allowing the test to prove whether hook identity is captured in provenance without executing unknown or destructive code.
scenarios.toolchain_build_environment: Two synthetic toolchain or build-image identities differ only by a harmless deterministic marker, making it possible to test whether output and provenance remain bound to the intended toolchain identity.
scenarios.ci_principal_trust_context: Use explicit fake principals such as synthetic-untrusted-pr and synthetic-trusted-main, with policy declaring that only trusted-main output or an independently rebuilt artifact may enter the release candidate set.
scenarios.cache_reuse_input_binding: Local cache entries record producer trust class, source revision, dependency digests, toolchain identity, build-hook generation, and cache namespace so trust-separated and cache-disabled controls can be compared deterministically.
scenarios.produced_artifact_identity: The deterministic build emits an inert artifact digest plus a manifest of source, dependency, hook, toolchain, cache, workflow, and CI trust inputs, providing a direct produced-artifact identity for comparison.
scenarios.release_signing_publishing_authority: A fake local release authority accepts only produced artifacts whose provenance verifier marks the builder and inputs as trusted, and it never signs or publishes anything outside the local fixture.
scenarios.distributed_artifact_identity: If distribution is exercised, the artifact remains a local digest-addressed copy of the release candidate so the case can prove build/CI trust without introducing network or third-party distribution variables.
scenarios.deployed_runtime_artifact_identity: The bounded deployment target records only the inert artifact digest and provenance status, avoiding execution of synthetic dependency code while still proving which build output would be accepted.
scenarios.bounded_effect: The strongest allowed effect is a changed local build digest or acceptance/rejection decision in the synthetic release fixture; no real release, external upload, secret use, or production deployment occurs.
scenarios.lifecycle_revocation_update_generation: Advance a synthetic build-policy or toolchain generation after one run and verify stale cache/provenance state does not continue granting trusted status when the current generation requires different inputs.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Keep source and dependency identities fixed while varying exactly one of build hook, toolchain identity, CI principal trust class, or cache provenance, then compare produced digest and verifier decision.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude harmless timestamp differences, platform-specific deterministic variation, resolver changes, stale local fixtures, cache-key defects delegated to the cache profile, and intentionally equivalent toolchain images before promotion.
scenarios.evidence_level: A directly observed provenance or trust-context mismatch supports SC1; two trust contexts collapsing to one accepted identity supports SC2; inert lower-trust artifact acceptance can support SC3 or bounded SC4 in the local release fixture.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Do not claim compromise of a real CI or release pipeline from this synthetic case; SC5 requires the complete trusted-build causal chain, remediation, regression, and bounded release/deployment binding within authorized scope.

scenarios.hypothesis: A produced artifact can become detached from release approval, fake signer/publisher authority, distribution identity, deployed identity, or current lifecycle generation, allowing a neighboring or stale synthetic artifact to remain accepted.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use digest-addressed inert local artifacts, fake signer and publisher identities, a deterministic release-policy simulator, local distribution storage, and a reversible deployment record containing only artifact metadata.
scenarios.positive_control: The intended produced digest, approved by the authorized fake release authority and current generation, must remain byte-identical through local distribution and be accepted by the bounded deployment fixture.
scenarios.negative_control: A neighboring digest, unauthorized fake signer, substituted distributed artifact, or artifact from an invalidated generation must be rejected while the legitimate current release and explicitly allowed rollback case still function.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop if validation would require a real signing key, live package or image publication, production CDN or update-service changes, real downstream installation, or replacement of a third-party or production artifact.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, approval, signature, publication, distribution, deployment, and lifecycle policy must bind the exact intended digest and current generation while preserving authorized release, update, and rollback behavior.
scenarios.declared_requirement: The fixture begins with a fully resolved synthetic build input set so this scenario can focus on the transition from produced artifact through release, distribution, deployment, and lifecycle state.
scenarios.source_resolution_policy: Dependency and source resolution policy is fixed and already validated by local evidence, preventing namespace or resolver ambiguity from masquerading as a release or distribution binding defect.
scenarios.selected_namespace_source: All selected package and source identities remain constant local fixtures during this case, and their immutable identities are included in the produced artifact provenance manifest for reference.
scenarios.selected_artifact_identity: The build input artifacts are digest-addressed and unchanged; the security-relevant identities under test are the produced release candidate, neighboring candidate, distributed copy, and deployed artifact digest.
scenarios.immutable_pin_integrity_state: Each candidate, release object, distributed object, and deployment record carries an exact digest, while the test deliberately varies authority or generation without relying on mutable names or tags as identity.
scenarios.provenance_verifier_decision: The local verifier checks that the release candidate digest matches trusted build provenance and that the release policy names the expected fake builder, signer, publisher, and current policy generation.
scenarios.install_build_hook: Build hooks are held constant and represented in the trusted produced-artifact provenance, ensuring release-chain observations are not explained by an earlier build-input change.
scenarios.toolchain_build_environment: The deterministic toolchain and build environment remain fixed to one immutable fixture identity throughout the scenario so release, distribution, deployment, and lifecycle state are the only changed variables.
scenarios.ci_principal_trust_context: The produced artifact is created by one trusted synthetic build principal, while release approval uses a distinct fake release principal so CI execution authority is not confused with release authority.
scenarios.cache_reuse_input_binding: Cache state is fixed, disabled, or proven trusted by local provenance before the scenario begins, preventing stale build cache from being mistaken for a release-artifact or lifecycle binding failure.
scenarios.produced_artifact_identity: Capture the exact deterministic release-candidate digest and its trusted provenance manifest, then compare every later approval, signature, distribution, and deployment record against that identity.
scenarios.release_signing_publishing_authority: A fake local release authority is permitted to approve and sign only the intended produced digest for the current generation, while a neighboring fake authority provides the negative authorization control.
scenarios.distributed_artifact_identity: The local distribution fixture stores and serves a digest-addressed inert artifact; substitution is simulated only by swapping to another local inert digest so distribution binding can be measured safely.
scenarios.deployed_runtime_artifact_identity: The reversible deployment fixture records the accepted artifact digest, release generation, and verifier result without executing the artifact, providing direct evidence of which distributed identity would become active.
scenarios.bounded_effect: The maximum effect is acceptance of the wrong inert local artifact metadata into a reversible deployment record or rejection of the intended candidate; no code execution, real publication, or production state is involved.
scenarios.lifecycle_revocation_update_generation: Advance a synthetic release or revocation/update generation after the artifact is initially valid, then verify stale approval, signature, distribution, deployment, and rollback decisions converge on the new generation policy.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold produced bytes constant while changing fake signer or generation, then separately hold authority constant while changing distributed digest, proving which transition causally controls release or deployment acceptance.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Exclude documented repackaging with an auditable digest chain, intentionally permitted rollback windows, mirror synchronization delay, stale fixture metadata, platform-specific artifact variants, and prior build provenance drift.
scenarios.evidence_level: Wrong local release or distribution identity acceptance supports SC2 or SC3 depending on the oracle; a reversible deployment decision using the wrong inert artifact can support SC4 when the full local causal path is captured.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: SC5 requires exact produced-to-released-to-distributed-to-deployed binding, current lifecycle generation, paired controls, alternative-explanation elimination, remediation, and regression; never extrapolate this fixture to real release infrastructure.
